John Moore likes a fight- at running that is! and set about the opposition as though he wanted revenge for Charlie. Seven went down for the count, and Jumbo Masters set off in a respectable sixth place.

After the half-way mark and turn for home, and two miles of down hill running to go, Brian Hallowell made full use of his long stride to improve his position in the nineties while John Moore and Chas Walker were leading him slightly.
Walker, in 12th spot, with John Moore a few yards further back, 18th. These four were well backed up by Eric Gebbett, 22nd, Clive Shippen, 30th Mal Robinson, 31st and Don Maclean in 40th position.
The furious pace set by Mac through the woods was too fast for John Moore, who dropped back to join Eric Gebbett and Clive Shippen fifty yards behind.

After 2½ miles Charlie was 5th, followed by Ken Miller 28th, David Jones 46th, Ranjit Bhatia 53rd, John Moore 60th, Clive Shippen 61st, and Ken Venton 82nd, with the others at regularly spaced intervals within the first half of the field.

John Moore had not been seen in action for some time and on the next leg it was soon quite clear he was not showing the form of last year. In the last half mile he had to give way to Mitcham which left us third with Highgate 56 secs ahead.

Going off down Copse Hill the three leaders were still locked together but the field behind had started to string out, although it was noticed that John Moore, Jim Radford and Archie Bedford who had started slowly were working their way through.

I dont think Charles had realised how long the hill is from Coulsdon to Hooley and it was a very tired Walker who handed over to John Moore at "The Joliffe" in tenth place, 2-34 behind Derby who were by now established at the front in what was to be a winning lead.

Approaching the mile post, John Moore began to fade, and a little afterwards Norton retired. On the fifth lap Bill was still leading, but noticeably struggling, and it was no surprise when Dabbs shot ahead in an effort to break up the pack—with two fast-finishing rivals alongside his only hope was t…

It was good to see John Moore back in club races, we need his help and hope he can regain his position of a year or two ago. The final times were disappointingly slow, probably due to the weather, but it was pleasing to see the leaders fairly well bunched.
Walker ran steadily in fourth position, John Davies showed a glimpse of his old form, and John Moore showed that he was beginning to find his feet again.
David Jones, making a welcome return to the running scene was 9th and John Moore, also fighting his way back, 10th. A gap of nearly 3 minutes separated these 10 from the rest of the field.

The end of the season coincided with the return to fitness of a previous'5¾' winner - John Moore. John is determined to make a successful come-back and hopes to do some road racing this summer for the first time in order to continue his progress.
Of our non-scoring runners, it was pleasing to see John Moore out again. Charlie Dabbs is fighting his way back and should he among the scorers next time.

The seventh and eighth legs were taken by reserves, and although both John Moore and David Jones flogged themselves to the utmost, they were not really fit enough for this type of competition, and we had to drop back to ninth some 6 mins. behind Portsmouth when Barry Sawyer took over.
It was very encouraging to see John Moore once again out on the road and approaching something like his old fitness. Also out that day were Norman Stairs, Ray Conway,and Charlie Manning.

John Moore had a steady run and Ron Linstead and Barry Sawyer consolidated our position amongst the leading four. Gerry North then took over for the penultimate stage and showed everyone what a great road-runner he is by smashing Hogan's course record by 9 seconds, to record a fantastic 12:38.

New faces are always welcome and this season the road running ranks have been swelled by Gerry North, Bill Kerr, Charlie Walker, George Williams John Moore and Peter Wrench; and with Jack Brown showing a return to form, things look good for next season.

Another junior, Chris Steer, also performed well to finish 55th with John Moore 59th and David Jones 89th. These were the scoring four who amassed 222 points as compared with Guildford and Godalming's 81.
John Moore and Derek Crookes were running together a little further back and it was clear we would finish 6 in 40 despite the retirement of John Thresher and Bill Kerr.

David Jones was nowhere near his recent form and John Moore, inexcusably, was left at the start. Charlie Walker ran well and moved through the field with great determination---fast catching Alan at the finish.

Great running by Barry and thorough justification of his relentless training. Fine return to form by John Moore and as they say in 'Juke Box Jury' "The backing" was well provided by the two Bishops - L. & A.

From left to right, Norman Stairs, Barry Sawyer, Alan Bishop, Len Bishop, John Moore, Charlie Walker, Denis Jones, and Derek Crookes. This picture was taken at Windsor Castle just before they were sent on their way by Her Majesty The Queen.
John Moore had a fine run in the Southall '10' on September 7th finishing 3th in 54:12.
Of our other runners Barry Sawyer, Charlie Dabbs and John Thresher performed well and John Moore was also prominent in a very strong field. A Club handicap was held in conjunction and D.C.

With John Moore then 20th, Dave Cocks 49th and Jackie Hampshire moving through in the 70's, there was still an outside chance of a team place, but Chris then had a bad bout of "stitch" which sent him back 40 places in the space of a mile, and with our other runners roughly holding their positions we…

John Moore (157th) ran for Middlesex and was Belgrave's only representative On a five-to-score basis the 'inter-club' result would have been Portsmouth AC 149, Surrey AC 204, Derby 208, Coventry 231 and Bristol 295.

John Moore got a fair start and fought well to hold on to his place as last man in the County team (9th). Pat Newell backed up well and was always in the early 'teens but failed, for the umpteenth time, to get that County vest.
John Moore and Chris Steer moved thro8 in great style only just failing to catch Thresher. Twenty-five seconds covered 5 scorers after Dabbs - packing which no one could match.

John Moore set off on stage 2 (4½ miles) behind Salvat of Portsmouth and the Ryde runner. He soon passed the latter but could make no impression on the 'bearded wonder' who is a very seasoned campaigner and always a difficult opponent.

Stage V, John Moore (21:46 - 8th fastest) John's time lowered the club record by 3 secs. yet even this was not good enough to gain on the leaders or to hold Edmonds of Bristol at bay, and at the end of the stage we were 2 mins 20 secs. behind back to eighth position.
We could only field three runners, Charlie Walker 18th (83:37), John Moore 27th (84:50) and Alan Bishop 77th (92:00). Derby were the winners with 14 points and Belgrave 8th with 89 points.
John Moore finished 17th in the All-Ireland C.C.

A weak Belgrave team ran in this year's Chichester to Portsmouth '16'and could only finish 15th. John Moore was the first Belgravian home with 1:30:43 in 18th position.
John Moore was placed 6th at '20' with Stairs still behind him,but he faded a little,though,to put up the creditable time of 2:45:54 in 8th place over a very tough course.

John Moore and Norman Stairs had been backing up well and they finished strongly in 22nd and 24th positions with personal best times. Charlie Walker completed our scoring three,but with a time of 5mins slower than last year.

There were 102 starters,and Pat Newell was soon up with the leaders, followed closely by John Moore. At 10 miles last year's runner up,Wright of Derby, had taken a lead of 2¼ mins and looked all over a winner - Pat Newell was 4th and John Moore 8th

Gerry North,Batty and Price went straight to the front,and Mel Thorpe and John Moore were soon dogging their heels. Half-way round the 10miles 700yd course Gerry just led from the Thurrock man,with the remainder well down.
Norman Stairs ran a sound race to finish 39th and John Moore,still striving to get fit after his recent illness,completed our scoring 'A' team in 54th place.
Mel Thorpe had a great race finishing 5th,and the ever-present Charlie Walker completed our scoring team in 22nd place. John Moore,Ken Stimpson and John Baker also enjoyed an outing.

After going through 15miles in just over 84mins. he began to slow down quite a bit and John Moore, now beginning to get a little fitter, passed Charlie at about 21 miles and went on to take the Belgrave Championship Geoff Pearson and John Hilton ran well throughout John finishing in a personal best time.
From the Belgrave point of view it was encouraging to see Chris Steer running so well and John Moore now getting slowly back to somewhere near his best.

The penultimate leg was taken by John Moore, another to have had a below-form winter, and although he recorded a mediocre time he took us past Polytechnic into 3rd place only 46seconds behind Cambridge Harriers.
